speaker: Unknown
en: Low quality code can have compounding failures.
zh: 低质量代码可能导致复合失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we think that the same will be true with context where so much of the end result will be dictated by the quality of the context that we hand to our agents, particularly as they work more autonomously.
zh: 而我们认为，同样的道理也适用于上下文，最终结果在很大程度上将取决于我们交给智能体的上下文质量，尤其是当它们更加自主地工作时。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's going to create this flywheel effect where high quality context results in good outcomes, which becomes tomorrow's high quality context.
zh: 这将产生一种飞轮效应：高质量上下文带来好的结果，而这些结果又成为明天的高质量上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on the flip side, crappy context will result in bad outcomes that will feed future bad agent interactions.
zh: 反过来，糟糕的上下文会导致糟糕的结果，进而影响未来糟糕的智能体交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome to the Engineering Enablement Podcast.
zh: 欢迎收听 Engineering Enablement 播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm your host this week, Brian Houck.
zh: 我是本周的主持人 Brian Houck。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we jump into the episode, I want to tell you about the CAFES framework, a new research paper co-authored by researchers from DX, Capital One, GitHub, University of Victoria, and Google.
zh: 在进入本期节目之前，我想向你们介绍 CAFES 框架，这是一篇新的研究论文，由来自 DX、Capital One、GitHub、维多利亚大学和 Google 的研究者共同撰写。

speaker: Unknown
en: It explores why context quality has become the central bottleneck in agentic workflows and introduces five properties to help teams make their AI agents more effective.
zh: 它探讨了为什么上下文质量已成为智能体工作流的核心瓶颈，并引入了五个属性，帮助团队让他们的 AI 智能体更加高效。

speaker: Unknown
en: When teams provide better context, they build more effective agents and achieve far better engineering outcomes.
zh: 当团队提供更好的上下文时，他们能构建更高效的智能体，并取得远更好的工程成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: To learn more and read the paper, head over to getdx.com forward slash cafes.
zh: 要了解更多信息并阅读论文，请访问 getdx.com forward slash cafes。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you, everyone, for joining today.
zh: 感谢大家今天参加。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely thrilled to be talking about a new paper, Cafes, that just was published this morning.
zh: 我非常兴奋能谈论一篇今天早上刚刚发表的新论文 Cafes。

en: And so it is perfect timing.
zh: 所以时机恰到好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: The stars aligned.
zh: 星象都对齐了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am thrilled to be joined by my Cafes co-authors today, who I'll ask to introduce themselves in just a second.
zh: 我很高兴今天有我的 Cafes 合著者加入，我稍后会请他们做自我介绍。

speaker: Unknown
en: But to kick us off,
zh: 但作为开场，

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Brian Houck.
zh: 我是 Brian Houck。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am your host today.
zh: 我是今天你们的主持人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am one of the resident mad scientists over here at DX, studying all things developer productivity, and I will hand it over to Max.
zh: 我是 DX 这里的常驻疯狂科学家之一，研究开发者生产力的方方面面，接下来交给 Max。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, everybody.
zh: 大家好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am Max Canet-Alexander, and I am a principal software engineer at Capital One, where I help lead Capital One's efforts around AI-assisted software development.
zh: 我是 Max Canet-Alexander，我是 Capital One 的首席软件工程师，在那里我帮助领导 Capital One 在 AI 辅助软件开发方面的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, I'm Irini.
zh: 你好，我是 Irini。

speaker: Unknown
en: I recently joined CX as a researcher as of like three days ago.
zh: 我最近刚加入 CX，成为一名研究员，大概三天前的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when I worked on this paper, I was at GitHub as a research advisor.
zh: 但在我做这篇论文的时候，我在 GitHub 担任研究顾问。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's what we'll talk about today.
zh: 所以这就是我们今天要谈论的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm Margaret Ann.
zh: 我是 Margaret Ann。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody calls me Peggy.
zh: 大家都叫我 Peggy。

speaker: Unknown
en: Story from the University of Victoria.
zh: 故事来自维多利亚大学。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been studying developer experience and how developers use tools for a long time.
zh: 我研究开发者体验以及开发者如何使用工具已经很长时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've worked a lot with Brian and Irini on these very topics and chatted a lot with Max.
zh: 我和 Brian 以及 Irini 在这些话题上合作过很多，也和 Max 聊过很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is the first time we've actually worked together.
zh: 所以这是我们第一次真正一起合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thrilled to be working with Max and all of you as well on this framework.
zh: 所以能和 Max 以及你们所有人一起做这个框架，我感到非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also would like to point out that we had the great privilege of having Dr. Nicole Forsgren be a co-author on the paper.
zh: 我还想指出，我们有幸邀请到 Dr. Nicole Forsgren 担任这篇论文的合著者。

speaker: Unknown
en: She unfortunately couldn't join us today for the panel, but was a key contributor to the paper itself.
zh: 她很遗憾今天无法参加这个座谈，但她是这篇论文本身的关键贡献者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, Nicole, if you are watching this, we are thinking of you for sure.
zh: 所以，Nicole，如果你在看这个，我们肯定在想着你。

speaker: Unknown
en: With that, I'm going to give a little bit of background on what Cafes even is, what's the problem space we are looking at before I kick off a round of questions with my fabulous co-authors.
zh: 说了这些，我准备稍微介绍一下 Cafes 到底是什么、我们正在关注的问题空间是什么，然后我会和我出色的合著者们开始一轮问答。

speaker: Unknown
en: CAFES is a framework ultimately for measuring the health and quality of the context that we are feeding into our AI agents.
zh: CAFES 归根结底是一个用于衡量我们喂给 AI 智能体的上下文的健康度和质量的框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I firmly believe that if we want to improve, maximize AI agent effectiveness, we have to have ever increasingly better context.
zh: 而我坚信，如果我们想提升、最大化 AI 智能体的效能，我们就必须拥有不断提升的更好的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: As I sort of think about like, what do I mean by context and how does it fit in sort of like human agent collaboration?
zh: 当我思考上下文的含义以及它在人类与智能体协作中如何定位时，

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I sort of trace this from left to right, ultimately intent is what it is a human wants to accomplish.
zh: 当我从左到右梳理这个流程时，归根结底，意图就是一个人想要完成的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that intent has to be translated into context, which is
zh: 而这个意图必须被转化为上下文，也就是

speaker: Unknown
en: The task that you want to complete, all of the information, the constraints, the data associated with it, your code, that's the context.
zh: 你想要完成的任务、所有相关的信息、约束、数据、你的代码，这些就是上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of the information, the knowledge that we are passing to our agents, which gets orchestrated through our harnesses, which deal with retrieval and memory and execution logic before ultimately passing it to the models, which supply the underlying intelligence.
zh: 我们传递给智能体的所有信息和知识，通过我们的 harness 进行编排，harness 处理检索、记忆和执行逻辑，最终传递给模型，由模型提供底层智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, if we want to maximize our human agent collaboration, get the most out of our agents, everything in this flow is important.
zh: 现在，如果我们想最大化人类与智能体的协作，从我们的智能体中获得最大收益，这个流程中的一切都很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like everything has to get better.
zh: 一切都必须变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we already spend enormous effort improving our harnesses through harness engineering, improving our models through sort of like frontier development.
zh: 但我们已经花费了巨大的精力通过 harness 工程改进我们的 harness，通过前沿开发改进我们的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Intent, we improve through improving our product planning processes to better synthesize and think about customer data, excuse me, things of that nature.
zh: 意图方面，我们通过改进产品规划流程来提升，以便更好地综合和思考客户数据，抱歉，诸如此类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what I found is that almost nobody is holistically evaluating the quality of context itself.
zh: 但我发现，几乎没有人对上下文本身的质量进行整体评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is so important right now, especially because of a variety of compounding risks that low quality context in our agentic workflows puts onto us.
zh: 而这一点现在如此重要，尤其是因为低质量上下文在我们的智能体工作流中给我们带来了各种复合风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: One example of that is just liability.
zh: 其中一个例子就是责任问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Organizations are being held accountable for what their agents say and do.
zh: 组织正在为其智能体的言行承担责任。

speaker: Unknown
en: If your chat agent
zh: 如果你的聊天智能体

speaker: Unknown
en: Hallucinates a sale that doesn't really exist.
zh: 幻觉出一个并不真实存在的促销活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Courts have helped that you are responsible for honoring that.
zh: 法院已经帮助你(裁定)你要为兑现它负责。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cost.
zh: 成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: We all see costs skyrocketing.
zh: 我们都看到成本在飙升。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is growing exponentially.
zh: 它在呈指数级增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, every token has a cost associated with it.
zh: 而且,你知道,每个 token 都有与之相关的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And context is really where those costs accumulate.
zh: 而上下文正是这些成本累积的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is everything that you are asking your agents to read and what you are having them produce is all a function of the context.
zh: 你要求智能体去阅读的一切,以及你让它们产出的一切,全都是上下文的函数。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also developer experience.
zh: 还有开发者体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we are seeing, even though we are accomplishing more, we are building more and more and more than ever,
zh: 就像我们看到的那样,尽管我们完成了更多的事情,我们正在建造比以往任何时候都更多、更多的东西,

speaker: Unknown
en: We're seeing some downward pressure on developer experience.
zh: 我们却看到开发者体验承受着向下的压力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Annie Vella has called this the productivity experience paradox.
zh: Annie Vella 把这称为生产力体验悖论。

speaker: Unknown
en: And part of that is because poor context turns AI into not something that's helping us, it's turning AI into another source of developer toil.
zh: 其中一部分原因是,糟糕的上下文把 AI 变成了不是在帮助我们的东西,而是把 AI 变成了另一个开发者苦役的来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are lots of ways that our context fails us.
zh: 而我们的上下文辜负我们的方式有很多种。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so like, what does it mean to have bad context?
zh: 那么,拥有糟糕的上下文意味着什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, let's talk through just some examples of named real world failures that result from having bad context beyond just hallucination, which is what oftentimes we talk about.
zh: 好的,让我们来过一遍一些有名字的、由糟糕上下文导致的真实世界失败案例,而不仅仅是我们经常谈论的幻觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first example is what we call weekend runaway, which is like you may set your agents about on a task Friday afternoon and you don't clearly define what done means.
zh: 第一个例子是我们所说的「周末狂奔」,就是说你可能在周五下午派你的智能体去执行一个任务,而你没有清楚地定义「完成」意味着什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so those agents just keep going and going and going and going, expanding their scope.
zh: 于是那些智能体就一直在做、一直做、一直做、一直做,不断扩大它们的范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you don't realize that until you come in on Monday morning and you see that you've blown through your entire month's token allocation.
zh: 而你直到周一早上进来时才意识到,你已经烧光了整个月的 token 配额。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ambiguity.
zh: 模糊性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agents don't stop to negotiate requirements.
zh: 智能体不会停下来去协商需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: They will pick an interpretation often silently and proceed often confidently.
zh: 它们通常会默默地选定一种解释,并常常充满自信地继续进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the problem is, if that first assumption is wrong early on, it just snowballs and compounds.
zh: 问题是,如果最初的那个假设在早期就是错的,它就会滚雪球般地不断叠加恶化。

speaker: Unknown
en: The next failure mode is what's called lost in the middle.
zh: 下一种失败模式叫做「迷失在中间」。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agents get distracted.
zh: 智能体会分心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you may have incredibly valuable, important, relevant context buried in a much larger context window.
zh: 所以你可能把极其有价值、重要、相关的上下文埋在了一个大得多的上下文窗口里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the agents may overlook the part that really matters because of placement.
zh: 而智能体可能仅仅因为位置的原因就忽略了真正重要的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: They truly get distracted.
zh: 它们是真的会分心。

speaker: Unknown
en: So oftentimes I hear people talk about like, how can we get larger and larger context windows?
zh: 所以我经常听到人们谈论,我们怎样才能获得越来越大的上下文窗口?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that is the wrong way to look at it.
zh: 而我认为那是一种错误的看待方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we had infinite size context windows, we may have substantially worse outcomes as a result because of lost in the middle.
zh: 如果我们拥有无限大小的上下文窗口,结果可能会因此糟糕得多,正是因为「迷失在中间」。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just the last example that I'll talk through real briefly is prompt injection.
zh: 我要简要讲到的最后一个例子是提示词注入。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, much like we have SQL injection, there are real world failure cases.
zh: 你知道,就像我们有 SQL 注入一样,存在着真实世界的失败案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where instructions were embedded in the context that the agent then acted on, resulting in sensitive information getting leaked, you know, perhaps even customer data getting leaked.
zh: 即指令被嵌入在上下文中,而智能体随后据此采取了行动,导致敏感信息被泄露,你知道,甚至可能是客户数据被泄露。

speaker: Unknown
en: And while like, yes, our harnesses and models may be able to help protect us against this, it doesn't change the fact that the underlying context itself was compromised.
zh: 虽然是的,我们的工具框架和模型也许能够帮助我们防范这种情况,但这改变不了底层上下文本身已经被攻破这一事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as we look at some of these named failure modes, the ways that context might fail, we thought about, well, what are all of the durable properties of high quality context?
zh: 所以,当我们审视这些有名字的失败模式、上下文可能辜负我们的种种方式时,我们思考了,那么高质量上下文的所有持久特性是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And the first is, is clarity, is, you know, can the agent interpret the request the way that you intended it to be interpreted?
zh: 第一个是清晰性,就是,智能体能按照你意图中想要被理解的方式来解读这个请求吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like ambiguity...
zh: 就像模糊性……

speaker: Unknown
en: is invisible to the person defining the task.
zh: 对于定义任务的人来说是不可见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We know what we meant, but thankfully, the agents don't live in our heads.
zh: 我们知道自己是什么意思,但庆幸的是,智能体并不活在我们脑子里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so clarity is a dimension that has to be specified.
zh: 所以清晰性是一个必须被明确规定的维度。

speaker: Unknown
en: The next dimension is actionability.
zh: 下一个维度是可执行性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you specified a clear goal that the agent can work for towards?
zh: 你有没有指定一个智能体可以去努力达成的清晰目标?

speaker: Unknown
en: Does the agent know when it is done or will it just keep on going forever?
zh: 智能体知不知道什么时候算完成,还是它会永远不停地做下去?

speaker: Unknown
en: And clear is not the same thing as sufficient.
zh: 而清晰并不等于充分。

speaker: Unknown
en: You may have a perfectly clear task that is impossible to act on because it is not actionable.
zh: 你可能有一个完美清晰的任务,却无法执行,因为它不具备可执行性。

speaker: Unknown
en: The third dimension of cafes is...
zh: cafes 的第三个维度是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Fidelity.
zh: 保真性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Truthfulness.
zh: 真实性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can the agent trust that the context is true relative to the task that it is trying to accomplish?
zh: 智能体能否相信上下文相对于它想要完成的任务是真实的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And accuracy, truthfulness is actually a pretty hard property to wrap your mind around because we all have different definitions sometimes.
zh: 还有准确性,真实性其实是一个很难理解的属性,因为我们每个人对它的定义有时都不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And accuracy is not a property you set once.
zh: 而准确性不是一个你设置一次就完事的属性。

speaker: Unknown
en: It decays over time.
zh: 它会随时间衰减。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've seen this with existing documentation where an organization, maybe your organizations, have tons of documentation.
zh: 我们在现有文档中就见过这种情况,一个组织,也许就是你们的组织,有海量的文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if they were written two years ago, are they still relevant?
zh: 但如果这些文档是两年前写的,它们还有效吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you trust them?
zh: 你能信任它们吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that functionally the same thing as not having any documentation at all?
zh: 这在功能上是不是等同于完全没有文档?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the accuracy of that documentation is part of the very definition of the context quality.
zh: 所以这些文档的准确性本身就是上下文质量定义的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fourth dimension...
zh: 第四个维度……

speaker: Unknown
en: Is efficiency?
zh: 是效率?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is the context lean enough to be usable and affordable?
zh: 上下文是否足够精简,既可用又可负担?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I want to note that this doesn't necessarily mean the smallest possible context.
zh: 我想指出的是,这并不一定意味着尽可能小的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: It means the highest signal to noise.
zh: 它意味着最高的信噪比。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a place where, within your organizations, you see individual outliers and token usage.
zh: 而这也是一个地方,在你的组织内部,你会看到个别异常值和 token 使用情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oftentimes, it's a failure in efficiency, where it's like, oh, I want to...
zh: 通常,这是效率上的失败,比如,哦,我想……

speaker: Unknown
en: Help understanding this single method, and so I passed in my entire repo.
zh: 帮忙理解这一个方法,于是我把整个代码库都传进去了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or it's like, hey, I'm trying to debug this one failure, so I passed in all of my build logs.
zh: 或者是,嘿,我正在调试这一个失败,所以我把所有的构建日志都传进去了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every time you do that, the agents have to read it, and that just uses tokens.
zh: 而每次你这么做,智能体都得去读它,这就只是消耗 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the last property that we think defines what it means to be high-quality context...
zh: 然后是我们认为定义高质量上下文含义的最后一个属性……

speaker: Unknown
en: is security.
zh: 是安全性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that context safe and compliant?
zh: 那个上下文是否安全且合规?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the first four dimensions really talk about is the context itself high quality?
zh: 因此前四个维度讨论的是上下文本身是否高质量?

speaker: Unknown
en: The last dimension talks about should we have been using that context at all?
zh: 最后一个维度讨论的是我们是否一开始就应该使用那个上下文?

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, you may think, you may be asking yourselves, well, like, why these five dimensions?
zh: 现在,你可能会想,你可能会问自己,那么,为什么要这五个维度?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why not something else?
zh: 为什么不是别的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And ultimately, the principle that we had is a property
zh: 归根结底,我们所依据的原则是,一个属性

speaker: Unknown
en: Sort of gets its own pillar if it is not derivable from any of the others, if it can be acted on independently, and it names a real-world failure mode that the others miss.
zh: 如果它不能从其他任何属性推导出来,如果它可以被独立地行动执行,并且它指出了其他属性遗漏的一种真实世界的失败模式,那么它就有资格自成一柱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ultimately, we think these properties, if they are true, ultimately result in better context,
zh: 而归根结底,我们认为这些属性,如果为真,最终会带来更好的上下文,

speaker: Unknown
en: Which results in more effective agents, which ultimately results in what we care about better outcomes.
zh: 这会带来更有效的智能体,而最终带来的是我们真正关心的更好的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, that was a seven-minute overview of a very long paper.
zh: 再说一次,那只是一篇很长论文的七分钟概述。

en: And code review...
zh: 而代码审查……

speaker: Unknown
en: has taken the industry sort of decades to normalize if we ever have.
zh: 花了整个行业几十年来使之常态化，如果我们曾经做到的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Documentation work is often one of the first things that developers cut when they feel time pressure.
zh: 文档工作往往是开发者在感到时间压力时最先砍掉的东西之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone likes to have documentation.
zh: 每个人都喜欢有文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one likes to write it.
zh: 没有人喜欢写文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: My question to you is, as a real-world practitioner on the panel, is context review actually realistic?
zh: 我的问题是，作为 panel 上的一个真实世界从业者，上下文审查真的现实吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a great question.
zh: 这是个好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the goal that you should have is to have great context.
zh: 所以你应该有的目标是拥有很棒的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: Regardless of how you get there, that's what you're trying to accomplish.
zh: 不管你如何达到那里，那就是你想要实现的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are times when putting a human review gate in front of that process actually causes you to have lower quality context.
zh: 而有时候，在这个流程前面加一道人工审核关卡，反而会导致你的上下文质量更低。

speaker: Unknown
en: We saw this for years with documentation, where if you allow people to do very easy low review or no review documentation updates, you get a lot higher quality documentation because people all over the company, they'll just show up and they'll fix your documentation.
zh: 我们在文档上看到这种情况很多年了，如果你允许人们做非常容易的低审核或零审核的文档更新，你会得到质量高得多的文档，因为公司上下的人都会冒出来帮你修文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the other hand, there's also always been this same problem of there's a few types of documents or a few things that are so critical and so important and hard to get right and require expertise that somebody has to control what goes in there.
zh: 另一方面，也一直存在同样的问题，就是有少数几类文档或少数几样东西是如此关键、如此重要、如此难以做对、需要专业知识，以至于必须有人控制什么能放进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it has to be the person who has the expertise or the skill required in order to control the quality of that thing.
zh: 而且必须是由拥有相应专业知识或技能的人来控制那件东西的质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so basically your goal is to do whatever gets you that quality, but sometimes there are things that are so critical and in particular usually can only be correctly done by a small group of people or even sometimes a single individual.
zh: 所以基本上你的目标是做任何能带来质量的事，但有时候有些东西是如此关键，尤其是通常只能由一小群人、甚至有时是单独一个人才能正确完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they are the person who has like all of the business knowledge in order to make sure that that thing is saying the right thing, that you really would benefit from having a fixed and specific review process that is controlled and enforced on those things.
zh: 因为他们就是拥有全部业务知识、能确保那件东西说的是正确内容的人，这种情况下你真的会受益于一个固定且具体的审核流程，对这些东西加以控制和强制执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thinking about code review, I mean, code review was done, you know, to check the quality of the code, also to make sure that it could be maintainable and easy to change in the future.
zh: 所以想想代码审查，我是说，做代码审查是为了检查代码的质量，也是为了确保它在未来可维护、易于修改。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when we asked developers, like, what was one of the main benefits that they got from doing code review?
zh: 但当我们问开发者，做代码审查带给他们的主要好处之一是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was shared understanding.
zh: 是共享的理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right, about what the code is doing.
zh: 对，关于代码在做什么的共享理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that if we have a context review, say in a retrospective, that one of the things that we'll get from it is this shared understanding and this collective evaluation.
zh: 而且我认为，如果我们有一个上下文审查，比如说在复盘会里，我们从中得到的东西之一就是这种共享的理解和集体的评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is this enough context?
zh: 这个上下文够吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is this the right context?
zh: 这是对的吗上下文？

speaker: Unknown
en: But also kind of shared across people.
zh: 而且也是在人与人之间共享的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They know what it is that we're trying to do.
zh: 他们知道我们要做的是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I just wanted to mention that as well.
zh: 所以我只是想把这个也提一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I will say like in the paper, we go into much more depth on like what are sort of real world recommendations for validating and improving the quality of your context.
zh: 我还要说，在论文里，我们对如何验证和提升你上下文质量的现实世界建议做了深入得多的探讨。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I think, you know, we talked about code review and code quality, like so much about the quality of our resulting software has historically been dictated by the quality of the code that makes it up.
zh: 因为我觉得，你知道，我们谈了代码审查和代码质量，历来我们最终软件的质量在很大程度上是由构成它的代码质量决定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Low-quality code can have compounding failures.
zh: 低质量的代码会产生复合性的失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we think that the same will be true with context, where so much of the end result will be dictated by the quality of the context that we hand to our agents, particularly as they work more autonomously.
zh: 而且我们认为上下文也会是同样的情况，最终结果在很大程度上将由我们交给智能体的上下文质量决定，尤其是当它们更自主地工作时。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's going to create this flywheel effect where...
zh: 而且这会创造出一种飞轮效应……

speaker: Unknown
en: High quality context results in good outcomes, which becomes tomorrow's high quality context.
zh: 高质量的上下文带来好的结果，而好的结果成为明天的高质量上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on the flip side, crappy context will result in bad outcomes that will feed future bad agent interactions.
zh: 反过来，糟糕的上下文会带来糟糕的结果，而这些糟糕的结果会喂给未来糟糕的智能体交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there is this compounding value to improving your context now.
zh: 所以现在就改进你的上下文是有这种复合价值的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was going to make the same point about leverage, right?
zh: 我本来也想就杠杆讲同样的观点，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, because you asked the question, is this realistic?
zh: 因为，你问的这个问题是，这现实吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think keeping in mind that it's realistic if it's proportionate is what makes sense here.
zh: 而我认为要记住，只要成比例它就是现实的，这才是这里说得通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the discipline that we're talking about is there's a small set of things that every agent on the team reads, whether it's instructions or architecture docs and so on.
zh: 就是我们说的这种纪律，团队里每个智能体都会读的东西只有一小部分，无论是说明文档还是架构文档等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where the leverage is.
zh: 而杠杆就在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you get that right, then every agent becomes more capable with each right.
zh: 如果你把那部分做对了，那么每改对一次，每个智能体都变得更能干。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you get that wrong, then the same mistake runs in every session.
zh: 如果你把那部分做错了，那么同样的错误会跑在每一个会话里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think the effort is supposed to travel where the impact is, which is something that we also applied to code today.
zh: 所以我认为，精力应该流向影响所在之处，这也是我们今天对代码同样适用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't give the same review and attention to a throwaway script versus something that is a shared library.
zh: 对于一个一次性脚本和一个共享库，你不会给予同样的审查和关注。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I do think that keeping that proportionality and the where's the leverage, I think makes sense as a criteria.
zh: 所以我确实认为，保持这种比例感和追问杠杆在哪里，我认为作为一条准则是说得通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with that, we are just about at time.
zh: 说到这里，我们的时间差不多到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would like to thank all of my panelists and co-authors for joining me today.
zh: 我要感谢今天所有参加的嘉宾和共同作者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Please go and read the paper.
zh: 请大家去读这篇论文。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let us know what you think.
zh: 让我们知道你们的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'd like to know, like, does it actually match your real-world lived experiences?
zh: 我们想知道，比如，它是否真的符合你们现实世界中的亲身经历？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, do you find it relevant for what you're thinking about right now?
zh: 比如，你们觉得它与你们现在正在思考的事情相关吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have any questions, feel free to forward them to
zh: 如果你有什么问题，欢迎把它们发到

speaker: Unknown
en: Brian, B-R-I-A-N, at team-gitdx.com.
zh: Brian,B-R-I-A-N,at team-gitdx.com。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like I said, we'll try to encapsulate all of these questions and answer them in a dedicated newsletter.
zh: 就像我说的，我们会试着把这些所有问题汇总起来，在一期专门的通讯里回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so thank you all so very, very much.
zh: 所以非常非常感谢大家。
